description: Machine-readable constraint registry for the MRRC terminal firmware (ESP32-C3). Every rule here is a trap this project already fell into once; the incident is named in sdd_ref so the next person can read what it cost instead of rediscovering it. severity: block = reject the edit (CI + pre-tool hook), warn = allow but surface, info = guidance printed by brief only. Kinds: pattern (regex scan), order (pattern A must appear before pattern B in one file), numeric (a captured number must stay under a bound).

rules.title: Wi-Fi and server credentials never enter a tracked file
rules.message: Credentials live only in the gitignored sdkconfig.defaults.local. A password committed here is a password in every fork and every release tarball, and this repo publishes source-only releases.

rules.title: heat_init() runs before anything reads the palette
rules.message: heat_init() fills the colour ramp. Read it before it has run and every waterfall row is black — the symptom looks like a canvas bug, which is why this cost an afternoon. Keep the init call above the first palette consumer.

selftest_sample.content:
static void heat_init(void){}
void setup(void){ lv_canvas_set_palette(img, 0, c); heat_init(); }

selftest_clean.content:
static void heat_init(void){}
void setup(void){ heat_init(); lv_canvas_set_palette(img, 0, c); }

rules.title: The uplink frame timeout stays at or below 500 ms
rules.message: Frames are 20 ms apart, so a frame that cannot be written in 100 ms cannot be followed by the next four either — that was the original bound, and it is still the right reasoning for the link. What it missed is the client: esp_websocket_client treats a failed write as fatal, and it serves TLS in both directions from one task, so a downlink burst can hold an uplink write for ~105 ms. At 100 ms that turned into a torn session mid-transmission (2026-11-24: sendfail=146 in 2 s, 'PTT released itself' again); at 400 ms the same test finishes with sendfail=0 and no disconnect. The bound is 500 ms so a future change cannot quietly go back to half a second, which is where the transmit loop degrades to 2 frames/s.

rules.title: One socket: /WSterminal, never the four-endpoint layout
rules.message: A single TLS/WS session carries control, RX, TX and spectrum (1-byte channel prefix). Reintroducing a second endpoint reintroduces the tear-down/rebuild settle gap at the start of every transmission, plus a second 32 KB heap of TLS state this chip cannot spare.

rules.title: PCM16 only — there is no Opus decoder in this image
rules.message: libopus was measured at 24 KB of heap and ~60% of the core on this C3 and was removed. The terminal declares pcm16 and the server widens its own 48 kHz bus down to it; a decoder here would be a regression of the one budget that has no headroom.

rules.title: Every NVS handle opens the "mrrc" namespace
rules.sdd_ref: main/mrrc_cfg.c (namespace mrrc); docs/provisioning.md 'Why NVS over Kconfig'
rules.message: There are three writers by design — app_main.c (volume, mic gain, step, filter), mrrc_net.c (session token), mrrc_cfg.c (provisioned SSIDs/passwords/server) — and they share one namespace so a single dump shows every key the terminal keeps. A second namespace strands keys exactly when a migration needs to find them.

rules.title: CONFIG_MRRC_PROFILE stays off in shipped defaults
rules.message: The profile switch prints link:/ws:/txlink:/ring()/batt= lines several times a second. It is a debugging instrument measured in CPU and UART time; ship it on and the measurement changes the thing being measured.

rules.title: LVGL is touched from taskLVGL (mrrc_ui.c) only
rules.message: LVGL has no internal locking. A draw call from the net or audio task corrupts the object tree in ways that show up minutes later as a frozen screen. Route it through mrrc_ui_* (which posts to taskLVGL) instead.

rules.title: No per-frame heap allocation in the audio or uplink path
rules.sdd_ref: docs/design-v1.md §4.3 ('largest' is the only number that matters)
rules.message: Buffers are static (.bss) because the largest free block, not total free heap, is what fails first here. 50 allocations a second turn a 40 KB largest block into 12 KB of fragments — measured, not theoretical.

rules.title: Task stacks come from named macros, not literals
rules.message: Stack budget is a measured quantity on this chip (free=49-58K, largest=36-48K). A literal in a call site is invisible to the budget table and to the next person who has to shrink something.

rules.title: Release is fire-and-forget
rules.message: The radio obeys the first release written. A verify loop after it costs hundreds of milliseconds of stuck carrier in the worst case and teaches the operator that the key is slow. Stuck-keyup detection belongs to the watchdog, not to the release path.

rules.title: Before touching the uplink, read why transmit used to tear the socket down
rules.message: Server skips downlink audio for a socket that holds the PTT; the device keeps a 100 ms frame timeout. Both halves are load-bearing: remove either and 'PTT releases itself' comes back on a mobile link. The symptom looks like a key problem, so read §6 before concluding anything.

rules.title: A behaviour change also changes the record
rules.message: Same change, same commit: docs/optimization-notes.md for a performance number, docs/transport-tuning.md for anything on the audio path, docs/provisioning.md for settings, docs/UI.md for layout, CHANGELOG.md + CHANGELOG.zh_CN.md for user-visible behaviour. Measure first; a number without its condition is a rumour.

rules.title: Every claim carries its measurement point, date and scenario
rules.message: Nine rules, V1–V9: V1 measurement point + date + scenario; V3 negative results are recorded, not deleted; V4 corrections are in place and dated; V5 status is a ladder (proposed → accepted → implemented → field-exercised → hardware-verified); V6 a number without conditions is a rumour; V8 when two measurements disagree, find the differing condition before discarding either. A statement that cannot meet V1 is marked `proposed`, not written as fact.
